   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right

in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not

From Martin O'Connell,BIRMINGHAM



Dear Sir,

I am writing to ask you if you
have ever come across a program
for the 48K ZX Spectrum which
enables colour screen dumps to
be sent to a colour printer.

I have recently purchased a Star
LC100 colour printer but I
cannot get it to print graphics
in different colours.

I currently own a 48K ZX Spec-
trum, a Plus D interface running
under Uni-Dos and a Star LC100
colour printer.I also have a +3.


I note from your advert in
FORMAT that you have been
producing software since 1987.
Therefore, I would also be
grateful if you could send me
details of other software you
have for the Spectrum or the +3
and a price list.

Thanking you in anticipation.

Yours faithfully,


Martin O'Connell

Brian Cavers to Martin O'Connell

Write to Datel Electronics,Govan
Road, Fenton Industrial Estate,
Fenton, Stoke-on-Trent, ST4 2RS.
They've advertised their colour
printer driver for the LC200. It
states it also works with the
"LC10" (sic) - I assume that is
a misprint for "LC100" but even
if not,I am sure Star would have
a standard compatibility for the
method of colour printing so it
should work with your model.

Price is a hefty `19.99. It is
stated to work with Dk'Tronics,
Ramprint or +2A or +3 printer
port. I am sure it would work
with the +D also but you might
like to ask them when ordering.


Finally, I am sending you our
OUTLET back issues list and our
order form so you can join in
the monthly fun and games and
swapping of info - or just order
a specific back issue!

                      - Brian

From Leslie Pollard, HERTS.

Dear Ron and Brian,

It has happened again! In some
years of OUTLETTING (and very
happily I might say) I have only
had two discs which threw up
sector error and refused to load
some program.The enclosed OUTLET
68 won't load SPENT.

A few years back, in a letter to
me commiserating on my baffle-
ment with some strange Spectrum
happening, you remarked that
some Spectrum actions border on
paranormal. How right you are!
Not that some of those strange
events are now understood, often
with OUTLET help.


It is a fact that all problems
other people have - I have had
with bells on. It is a tribe
feeling that is generated by you
both.

Anyway back to this strange
event. The returned disc when it
got to "M" SPENT, gave..

   24.:2 SECTOR error 200:3.

    ...I coudn't find line 200:3
anywhere.

I am rather busy and having a
slot, decided to copy the disc
for reading a few days later
whilst returning the disc. Now I
always use SHIMON YOUNG'S "The
Copier" do not know what I would
do without it!

Copying from Drive 1 to 2 when
it got to "SPENT" it stopped,
changed border colour and
ruminated.

Irritated, I know not why, I
took the source disc out a bit
and chamging my mind pushed it
home again. Wonder of wonders,
Lo and behold etc., it copied
the awkward program. It works
too! It made me think a bit, I
do sometimes!


I catted to Drive 2, and then
used Disciple P12 load and sure
enough - it loaded - both as p12
and as autoload "M"! However, it
still refuses to load on drive
1.


Brains of all brains (who says
flattery gets nowhere), can you
suggest why this happened? Also
if you have a wee bit of time, a
little dissertation on SECTOR
ERRORS would divert me and
possibly others as well. I for
one do not understand them.

I did think it might be the
Disciple; I do occasionally have
it refuse to recognise Drive 2 -
a quick clean of contacts nearly
always corrects this though. I
have checked out as best I can
and it seems OK.

Changing the subject, did you
know that the bright young man
Shimon Young is now at
University ? Also that his


brother Jack is as clever with
computers but has reneged from
Spectrums! What a pity but it
happens all the time. I do
wonder what on earth I would do
without mine.

Thanks again for all the good
issues; the annual sub is worth
the programs on just a few of
the months. I am sure I write
for all your "readers" when I
say that it is nice to know that
things are a bit better for you
presently.

          Best wishes,

         Leslie Pollard

Brian Cavers to Leslie Pollard

I can think of three causes of
sector errors...

 1.An error in DOS (the program
 controlling the drive)due to...

  (a) a design fault,ie.,a bug.

  (b) a temporary corruption in
  memory perhaps due to a fluc-
  tuation in mains electricity
  or some other program altering
  it.

 2.A physical blemish on the
 magnetic surface of the disc.

 3.The saving and loading drives
 are calibrated differently.


I suspect No.3 in your case...

The magnetic tracks recorded by
drives on discs have to be at a
specific position so that they
can be located and the data
thereon read back into the com-
puter when needed. As with any
machine they can only be accur-
ate within certain tolerances
and my guess is that your drive
is calibrated at the limits of
ours. Normally they load O.K.
but perhaps only just within the
borderline. By removing the disc
and pushing it back in it may
have just nudged the track over
by a thousandth of an inch or so
which may have been enough to
get it to load -all guesswork of
course!


This also explains why it loaded
on your drive 2. If your drive 1
is calibrated differently then
suppose only one side of a track
is being read. Although magnetic
signal strength might be weak,
it could still be good enough to
load and only show itself now
and again say, if the signal
strength is even weaker due to a
blemish on the disc...

    NORMAL               OFFSIDE
   H-E-A-D               H-E-A-D
   0000000            0000000
 D 1111111            1111111
 A 000000             000000
 T 0000   <-blemish-> 0000
 A 11111              11111
   1111111            1111111
   1111111            1111111


If the spindle or "key lug" that
fit into the back of the discs
on your drive 1 is worn ever so
slightly that might also be a
factor and would account for the
tiny change of position when you
re-inserted the disc. Even if it
is not worn, it must always vary
a finite amount - even if it is
only a millionth of an inch!

Incidentally, the error message
was for line 200 in the CONTENTS
BASIC - not in "SENT". It was
the loading instruction from the
line in CONTENTS that was
actually doing the loading when
the error occurred although the
line 200 itself would have been
overwritten by the time you
broke in.
                   - S. Holmes

From Malcolm Perry,KIDDERMINSTER

I have had a request from an
OUTLET reader in the Netherlands
asking about using the UniDOS
Command Codes 72 to 84.While the
handbook lists the codes with
functions it does not actually
tell you how they are used.

The Disciple handbook not only
lists their codes but also tells
you the registers to load with
specific data and setting up the
UFIA. This information is sorely
missing from the Unidos handbook
so if anyone has detailed info
on the Uni-DOS extension codes..

[STOP PRESS. MALCOLM NOW HAS THE
UNIDOS INFO WHICH WILL APPEAR IN
A FUTURE DRIVECHAT IN OUTLET.BC]

A second question to which I do
not know the answer was about
the "OCP Editor/Assembler and
Toolkit" Is it available and is
there a +D version (or possibly
will the MD version run on a +D?
I used to have the HiSoft Devpac
Assembler that had a Disciple
version.

Thanks for the note about the
error in your COMET mod [to save
object code as a ZX file]. I had
in fact found it and done the
mod.

Incidentally,I presume this pro-
gram is one of your own but I
cannot recall seeing it mention-
ed before or if available, cost
and so on.


Brian Cavers to Malcolm Perry

Oops!There seem to be one or two
misunderstandings here! First,If
you mean is the COMET assembler
written by me - no, it is a SAM
assembler written by Edwin Blink
and was reviewed in OUTLET 51
where I stated that in my view
it is the best SAM assembler of
all.

Second, my modification to it is
so that it will save object code
as ZX SPECTRUM code files to SAM
disc. You then pull out the SAM
disc and put it in your +D or
Disciple drive and load it into
your Spectrum to test. If it
crashes or needs modification
you can still have the listing
on the SAM screen!

It's a great way to develop code
as you can make quick mods and
test it immediately without all
that reloading of assemblers,
reloading source, altering,
printing out the listing,
resaving source and object, etc.

You do not RUN the code on SAM.
It is simply saved to a SAM disc
or a Disciple/+D disc as a ZX
Spectrum code file that can be
loaded straight into the Spect-
rum. As you know, SAM code will
not load into the Spectrum.

I developed the mod too late to
go into the SAM OUTLET before it
ended and a SAM file will not
duplicate properly on our +D.So,
here is the listing for anyone
else that wants it...

DIM N$(10): LET N$=a$,SAD=16384

FOR T=0 TO 3: FOR S=1 TO 10
READ AT PEEK SVAR 7,T,S,SAD:
FOR OF=0 TO 256 STEP 256: IF
MEM$(SAD+1+OF TO SAD+10+OF)<>N$
THEN NEXT OF:NEXT S:NEXT T:STOP
 POKE SAD+OF,4
 POKE SAD+OF+211,3:
 POKE SAD+OF+218,0
DPOKE SAD+OF+214,adr
DPOKE SAD+OF+212,lngth
DPOKE SAD+OF+219,0

LET FT=PEEK(SAD+OF+13),
FS=PEEK (SAD+OF+14)
WRITE AT PEEK SVAR 7,T,S,SAD
READ AT PEEK SVAR 7,FT,FS,SAD:
POKE SAD,3: DPOKE SAD+1,8
DPOKE SAD+3,adr: DPOKE SAD+7,0
WRITE AT PEEK SVAR 7,FT,FS,SAD


The routine should work with any
SAM assembler and is entered...

IMMEDIATELY AFTER YOU HAVE SAVED
THE OBJECT CODE AND WITH...

    THE FILENAME IN a$

    THE FIRST ADDRESS IN adr

    THE LENGTH IN lngth

I urge you to test it first on a
spare unimportant disc in case
of any typing error because it
does write direct to the direct-
ory sectors and may corrupt a
disc if you type something wrong
(once confirmed, it is safe). It
can be put in a procedure or GO
SUB and the sector address of
16384 can be anywhere you want.

I can trace no supplier of the
OCP assembler at all. Your best
bet is to put a message into
OUTBOARD to buy one secondhand.

It is extraordinary that the UNI
DOS manual lists the command
codes without details of entry
registers etc.!What use are they
without them! However, I'm glad
to hear you finally got the info
and thanks for sending it in. I
shall put it in a future DRIVE-
CHAT so everyone can have the
benefit.
                        - Brian

should I try another assembler?

Brian Cavers to Mr. R.W. Whittle


Please let me know EXACTLY how
it crashes, e.g., do you enter
the J,NAME command, the drive
operates and then the computer
just locks up or can you load a
source file OK, examine it but
it crashes when you try to edit.

From what you say, I suspect the
latter but what kind of crash?
Does it just lock up, reset, is
there anything significant on-
screen?

Does it ALWAYS do it on EVERY
source file? If unsure, try
entering a file with just a RET
and see if it will reload OK.


Please send me a disc with one
of your source files that you
know will not load properly plus
a copy of your assembler. Test
the actual disc before sending
it to me to make sure you really
cannot load THAT source file
into THAT assembler on THAT disc
and edit it. I will return your
disc(with a new copy of JACKSOFT
if necessary). Tell me the EXACT
command you entered to save and
load the source code in case it
is possible to somehow get this
wrong and still save.

Have you made any changes to the
BASIC or code at all?If in doubt
load the original, enter a line
or two, save it, reset, reload

The only other thing I can think
of is if it is something to do
with the +2A but the +3 version
(the +3 has the same board as
the +2A) is OK and I don't
remember any changes having to
be made other than the usual
syntax changes.

I see no reason why we won't be
able to get it to work for you
but, if not, you might consider
DR. KODE [OUTLET 39] which is
another excellent assembler.

                       - Brian

rest of the circuit board by an

From Brian Birkett, CO.DURHAM


Dear Brian,

As feedback to your help regard-
ing my printout problem[OUTLETT-
ERS 68], you were correct that I
cannot seem to easily control
the problem by trying to alter
the text height from the printer
manual but your suggestion to
break into Basic [in CONTENTS]
and to add a line.....

1607 POKE 64817,18

                ...did the trick
and managed to print one page...
on one page followed by a normal
form feed.


You can see from the printout
that whilst the POKE value 18
gave a cramped result, 20 was
easier to read but takes a
little more setting accurately
for top and bottom margins. The
only other observation was that
the heading 'Outletters'
overprints two lines as a result
of the linefeed, but I am happy
to live with that.

I am surprised to learn that
there could be an unseen problem
with 24-pin printers with char-
acters being some 0.5mm higher
than 8 pin characters. I await
readers response to this oddity
with interest as the printer I
use is on a more or less perman-
ent loan and if it proves less


than a great advantage over my
Epson-incompatible EPSON RX80/FT
and I had to return the Panason-
ic KX-P1124 24 pin,I would think
hard before purchasing a 24 pin
as a replacement.

I have also included this text
on disk, but please don't return
it as a matter of cause if you
are not replying, as it is not
cost effective for you to do so.
I would suggest,possibly through
publication of part of this
letter, that if contributers
require disks returning, they
could enclose a 2nd class stamp
for return of any material.This,
I am sure, will not be an
as-expensive outlay to an indiv-
idual as it is to you when


returning several per month. You
know the old addage "take care
of the pence ....... "

Thanks for your help.

            Brian.

Brian Cavers to Brian Birkett

Well,I'm pleased to hear that my
solution worked O.K. I shouldn't
dismiss 24-pin printers too soon
though as they may become the
new standard one day and anyway,
the printing of OUTLET text in
its special TABLOID form may be
rather unusual in that it needs
to really fit an exact number of
lines of text on each page. By
contrast, in most wordprocessors
you can define how many lines
you want on a page and it does
not normally matter exactly; so
long as the user is happy with
the space at top and bottom he/
she probably doesn't care if
there are 55 or 65 lines. Maybe.
Perhaps.


Like you, I would be interested
to hear from other readers with
24-pin printers as to whether
their 24-pin mode characters are
taller than the 8-pin and if it
causes any problems. I do have a
nagging memory that something
like this may have come up
before with TABLOID but if it
did then I didn't solve it at
that time!
                        - Brian

From Chris Oliver.

Edge connector crashes on the
Spectrum +2 with +D:-

I got really fed-up with the
system crashing virtually EVERY
time I attempted to Save to
tape. It was fairly obviously a
mechanical problem, caused by
movement or flexing of the case
from the brute-force required
to operate the Record/Play .
buttons. Close inspection
revealed two effects which
could be possible origins of
the problem:- a). flexing or
sagging of the front of the
casing. b). tilting, which
slightly raised the rear of the
casing and edge-connector.


SOLUTION,which effectively kill-
ed both the above birds with one
stone: glued a small extra foot
under the casing, right at the
front and directly beneath the
Record/Play buttons. I used a
small slice of pencil-rubber
("Eraser" for our American read-
ers) but anything would do.Care-
ful measurement shows that the
thickness required is precisely
3.3mm (or in English, an eighth
of an inch + a gnat's whisker).

It could be easiest to gradually
sand down your insert, until you
get a nice firm fit, with no
hint of rocking between the
original feet and your new one.
RESULT: fantastic reduction (so
far) in edge-wobble crashes.
                         - Chris

From Brian Cavers to all

Has anyone got one of those
VIDEO PLUS+ gadgets that set a
video recorder timer just by
entering the codes from a TV or
Radio Times? I must admit to
being curious although I cannot
afford one at the moment.

How good are they? Do they need
any inital programming to work
with one's particular video?

What especially puzzles me is
the method of encodement. I have
pondered this over and over but
cannot come to any conclusion.It
seems the codes(which range from
three-digit numbers up to about
eight-digit) must include the
following...

START MONTH
START DAY
START HOUR
START MINUTE

END HOUR      (this could be the
END MINUTE     length instead)

CHANNEL

How it can encode something like
a start time of 10.30pm on 26th
August and ending at 11.30pm on
Channel 3 (223026083) in only 3
digits I do not know. It might
reduce the minutes somewhat by
taking the nearest 5 minutes as
all program times seem to be so
listed. A look-up table seems a
possibility but would need about
30 million entries FOR EACH
CHANNEL by my estimate!

It must allow for more channels,
say 50, 60, a 100? This gives a
look-up table of 3 billion. I
suppose it is possible. I can't
see how else it can do it. When
you look at a program listed as
from 11am to 11.30am on 14th May
on Channel 3 and another program
of EXACTLY the same time and
length and date but on Channel 4
and one has a code of 619 and
the other is 99883228,it is hard
to see any relationship!

Come on, cryptology enthusiasts!
See if you can crack it - or at
least throw some light on it so
my brain can have a rest! I hate
mysteries.

Now for something completely
different...

This tip is really nicked off of
Chris Oliver and for all I know,
probably everybody else already
knew it but me...

One sometimes needs to know not
just a PEEK value but whether a
particular BIT is set in the
BYTE. This is useful for some
system variables etc. It is easy
from machine code but in BASIC I
have previously resorted to some
fairly messy calculations. BUT,
it can be done neatly with...

INT (N/128) for BIT 7, INT(N/16)
for BIT 4 etc.(reading bits from
left to right as 7 to 0), e.g.,
INT(PEEK 23611/16) is 12 in 48K
mode and 13 in 128K mode. Useful
or what?

Now here's a programming problem
I can't solve. Let's see if any
of you can!When saving data from
a program (such as a text file
from a wordprocessor or a file
from a database) on the +D and
Disciple, if a VERIFY is added
after the SAVE then if a file
with the same name is already on
the disc and the user answers N
then the SAVE is aborted but the
VERIFY continues - result a
"verification has failed" error.

This is because the system has
compared the alien file on the
disc with the one in memory and
if they are different then it
will not "verify". Here is one
solution I thought up on the SAM
Coupe but it does not work on a
+D...

Just before the SAVE, PRINT a
small marker in the INPUT zone
in "invisible" ink, e.g., white
INK on white PAPER.Anything will
do but you need to detect it
after so any easy one is CHR$143
- the big black square - but it
is invisible if the INK is the
same as the PAPER in the INPUT
zone. It also will not change if
the user changes the character
set. If you print it thus...

PRINT #0;AT 0,0;"X"

The "X"above should be the black
square but I can't print it with
this text compressor.

Now, if a same-name file already
exists, any "OVERWRITE?" message
will erase the black square.

You can detect if the square has
gone just after the SAVE using..

IF PEEK 20672=255 THEN GO TO(the
VERIFY line...)

However it is not enough to just
test if the SAVE was challenged;
the user might have answered Y!
This is the hard bit. How do you
tell if the user pressed Y or N?

I solved this on the SAM by PEEK
23560 which gives the CODE of
the last key pressed so...

IF PEEK 23560=CODE"Y" THEN GO TO
(the VERIFY line...)

     ...but on the +D,interrupts
are often enabled too quickly to
read the keypress!

I assume the +D has its own key-
reading routine and detects the
pressing of Y or N before one
fiftieth of a second has passed
and the next interrupt calls the
normal Spectrum ROM keyreading
routine (which stores the key-
press in 23560). Therefore the
results are intermittent. Some-
times you can detect the Y or N
afterwards but mostly not.

I can think of no other way and
suspect there is no way in BASIC
(possibly a few POKEs into DOS?)

In MASTERFILE, I ended up asking
the user "VERIFY Y/N?" so if he
or she enters Y when the SAVE
was aborted then hard luck! Can
anyone else think of a solution?
                         - Brian

I can think of three causes of sector errors...

1.An error in DOS (the program controlling the drive)due to...

(a) a design fault,ie.,a bug.

(b) a temporary corruption in memory perhaps due to a fluc- tuation in mains electricity or some other program altering it.

2.A physical blemish on the magnetic surface of the disc.

3.The saving and loading drives are calibrated differently.

I suspect No.3 in your case...

The magnetic tracks recorded by drives on discs have to be at a specific position so that they can be located and the data thereon read back into the com- puter when needed. As with any machine they can only be accur- ate within certain tolerances and my guess is that your drive is calibrated at the limits of ours. Normally they load O.K. but perhaps only just within the borderline. By removing the disc and pushing it back in it may have just nudged the track over by a thousandth of an inch or so which may have been enough to get it to load -all guesswork of course!

This also explains why it loaded on your drive 2. If your drive 1 is calibrated differently then suppose only one side of a track is being read. Although magnetic signal strength might be weak, it could still be good enough to load and only show itself now and again say, if the signal strength is even weaker due to a blemish on the disc...

NORMAL               OFFSIDE H-E-A-D               H-E-A-D

```text
   0000000            0000000
 D 1111111            1111111
 A 000000             000000
```

T 0000   <-blemish-> 0000

```text
 A 11111              11111
   1111111            1111111
   1111111            1111111
```

If the spindle or "key lug" that fit into the back of the discs on your drive 1 is worn ever so slightly that might also be a factor and would account for the tiny change of position when you re-inserted the disc. Even if it is not worn, it must always vary a finite amount - even if it is only a millionth of an inch!

Incidentally, the error message was for line 200 in the CONTENTS BASIC - not in "SENT". It was the loading instruction from the line in CONTENTS that was actually doing the loading when the error occurred although the line 200 itself would have been overwritten by the time you broke in. - S. DIM N$(10): LET N$=a$,SAD=16384

FOR T=0 TO 3: FOR S=1 TO 10 READ AT PEEK SVAR 7,T,S,SAD: FOR OF=0 TO 256 STEP 256: IF MEM$(SAD+1+OF TO SAD+10+OF)<>N$ THEN NEXT OF:NEXT S:NEXT T:STOP POKE SAD+OF,4 POKE SAD+OF+211,3: POKE SAD+OF+218,0 DPOKE SAD+OF+214,adr DPOKE SAD+OF+212,lngth DPOKE SAD+OF+219,0

IMMEDIATELY AFTER YOU HAVE SAVED THE OBJECT CODE AND WITH...

THE FILENAME IN a$

THE FIRST ADDRESS IN adr

THE LENGTH IN lngth

IF PEEK 20672=255 THEN GO TO(the VERIFY line...)

IF PEEK 23560=CODE"Y" THEN GO TO (the VERIFY line...)

Effect on inflation, adds (%increase * group weight)/1000

Therefore, contribution to inflation in first year =

```text
(8*47)/1000 = .376%
```

and in second year =

```text
((17.5-8)*47)/1000 = .4465%
```

Over two years this rounds down to .8%.Of course the weights may be even lower in a years time reducing the effect of this mea- sure on inflation even further.

If wages are indexed to inflat- ion it is likely they will get a .3% increase in the first year - giving a drop of .26% in income (about `17 to `20 per year). Then there's rail, water, and other increases on top of that!

```text
DIM N$(10): LET N$=a$,SAD=16384

FOR T=0 TO 3: FOR S=1 TO 10
READ AT PEEK SVAR 7,T,S,SAD:
FOR OF=0 TO 256 STEP 256: IF
MEM$(SAD+1+OF TO SAD+10+OF)<>N$
THEN NEXT OF:NEXT S:NEXT T:STOP

DPOKE SAD+OF+214,adr
DPOKE SAD+OF+212,lngth
DPOKE SAD+OF+219,0

LET FT=PEEK(SAD+OF+13),
FS=PEEK (SAD+OF+14)
WRITE AT PEEK SVAR 7,T,S,SAD
READ AT PEEK SVAR 7,FT,FS,SAD:
POKE SAD,3: DPOKE SAD+1,8
DPOKE SAD+3,adr: DPOKE SAD+7,0
WRITE AT PEEK SVAR 7,FT,FS,SAD
```

Эта процедура должна работать с любым ассемблером для SAM и вводится...

Это позволяет нам оценить вероятный эффект от этих увеличений на инфляцию. Daily Mail оценила его в 0,8% за два года. Вот как это рассчитывается:

Эффект на инфляцию, добавляет
(% увеличения * вес группы) / 1000

Следовательно, вклад в инфляцию в первом году =
(8*47)/1000 = 0,376%
и во втором году =
((17,5-8)*47)/1000 = 0,4465%

За два года это округляется до 0,8%. Конечно, веса могут быть еще ниже через год, уменьшая влияние этой меры на инфляцию еще больше.

Обещаны «специальные положения», но затронуты будут не только те, кто получает пособия.

В 1991 году средние расходы домохозяйств с валовым доходом от 125 до 150 фунтов в неделю составляли около 146 фунтов в неделю. Топливо и свет занимали около 7% от этой суммы.

8% от 7% — это 0,56%, поэтому даже тому, кто тратит 7% своего дохода на газ и электричество, потребовалось бы увеличение заработка на 0,56% (нетто), чтобы покрыть только эти расходы.

Если зарплаты индексируются с учетом инфляции, вероятно, они получат повышение на 0,3% в первый год, что даст падение дохода на 0,26% (около 17–20 фунтов в год). А потом еще сверху железная дорога, вода и другие повышения!
